nodes.name: r-colour Ramsey number
nodes.statement: One of the most classical (and notorious) problems in combinatorics is to estimate the $r$-colour Ramsey numbers $R_r(k)$, the minimum $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every $r$-colouring of the edges of the complete graph on $n$ vertices contains a monochromatic clique on $k$ vertices.
differentia: every $r$-colouring of the edges of the complete graph on $n$ vertices contains a monochromatic clique on $k$ vertices
also_stated_at: The $r$-colour Ramsey number $R_r(k)$ is the minimum $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every $r$-colouring of the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ on $n$ vertices contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$.

nodes.name: Ramsey's theorem and the Erdős–Szekeres bound
nodes.statement: Ramsey~\cite{R30} proved in 1930 that $R_r(k)$ is finite for every $k,r \in \mathbb{N}$, and a few years later his theorem was rediscovered in a famous paper of Erd\H{o}s and Szekeres~\cite{ESz35}, whose method gives the bound $R_r(k) \leqslant r^{rk}$.
nodes.statement_short: Ramsey numbers are finite, and the Erdős–Szekeres method gives $R_r(k) \le r^{rk}$.

nodes.name: Erdős' random-colouring lower bound
nodes.statement: This bound turns out to be not too far from the truth: Erd\H{o}s~\cite{E47} showed in 1947 that a random colouring gives an exponential lower bound on $R_2(k)$, and his proof can easily be adapted to show that $R_r(k)\geqslant r^{k/2}$.
conclusions: a random colouring gives an exponential lower bound on $R_2(k)$
nodes.statement_short: Random colourings give the exponential lower bound $R_r(k) \ge r^{k/2}$.

nodes.name: Abbott's product-construction lower bound
nodes.statement: When $r \geqslant 3$, this lower bound was significantly improved by Abbott~\cite{A72}, who combined Erd\H{o}s' colouring with a simple product construction to show that \begin{equation} c^{rk} \leqslant R_r(k) \leqslant r^{rk} \end{equation} for some constant $c > 1$.
nodes.statement_short: For $r\ge3$, a product construction gives $c^{rk} \le R_r(k) \le r^{rk}$ for some $c>1$.

nodes.name: Known bounds on $R_r(k)$
nodes.statement: c^{rk} \leqslant R_r(k) \leqslant r^{rk}
nodes.label: eq:Rrk:known:bounds

nodes.name: Quasi-polynomial improvement for $R_2(k)$ (Rödl, Thomason, Conlon, Sah)
nodes.statement: Progress on the upper bound has been much slower, except in the case $r = 2$, where the upper bound of Erd\H{o}s and Szekeres was improved by R\"odl (see~\cite{GR}) and Thomason~\cite{T88} in the 1980s, by Conlon~\cite{C09} in 2009, and by Sah~\cite{S23} in 2023, leading to a bound of the form $$R_2(k) \leqslant e^{- c(\log k)^2} 4^k$$ for some constant $c > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Successive improvements culminate in $R_2(k) \le e^{-c(\log k)^2}4^k$.

nodes.name: Exponential improvement for diagonal Ramsey (Campos–Griffiths–Morris–Sahasrabudhe)
nodes.statement: An exponential improvement was finally obtained in 2023 by Campos, Griffiths, Morris and Sahasrabudhe~\cite{CGMS}, who showed that $$R_2(k) \leqslant (4 - \varepsilon)^k$$ for some constant $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: $R_2(k) \le (4-\varepsilon)^k$ for some $\varepsilon>0$.

nodes.name: Gupta–Ndiaye–Norin–Wei bound
nodes.statement: The method of~\cite{CGMS} has since been adapted and optimised by Gupta, Ndiaye, Norin and Wei~\cite{GNNW}, who obtained the bound $$R_2(k) \leqslant 3.8^k.$$

nodes.name: Exponential improvement for multicolour Ramsey numbers
nodes.statement: For each $r \geqslant 2$, there exists $\delta = \delta(r) > 0$ such that $$R_r(k) \leqslant e^{-\delta k} r^{rk}$$ for all sufficiently large $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: For every fixed $r\ge2$, $R_r(k) \le e^{-\delta k} r^{rk}$ for large $k$: an exponential improvement on Erdős–Szekeres.
also_stated_at: We prove, for each fixed $r \geqslant 2$, that $$R_r(k) \leqslant e^{-\delta k} r^{rk}$$ for some constant $\delta = \delta(r) > 0$ and all sufficiently large $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.label: thm:Ramsey:multicolour

nodes.name: Book
nodes.statement: The book $(A,B)$ is the graph formed by removing the clique with vertex set $B$ from the clique with vertex set $A \cup B$; that is, it is the graph $H$ with vertex set $A \cup B$ and edge set $$E(H) = \big\{ uv : \{u,v\} \not\subset B \big\},$$
nodes.statement_short: The book $(A,B)$: the clique on $A\cup B$ minus the clique on $B$.

nodes.name: (t,m)-book
nodes.statement: We say that $H$ is a \emph{$(t,m)$-book} if $|A| = t$ and $|B|= m$, and the sets $A$ and $B$ are disjoint.

nodes.name: Off-diagonal multicolour Ramsey number
nodes.statement: Our plan is to find a monochromatic copy of $K_k$ (in an arbitrary $r$-colouring $\chi$ of $E(K_n)$) by first finding a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book, where $$t = \varepsilon k \qquad \text{and} \qquad m \geqslant e^{-t^2/8k} \, r^{-t} \cdot n \geqslant R_r(k,\ldots,k,k-t),$$ for some constant $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(r) > 0$, where $R_r(k_1,\ldots,k_r)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $E(K_N)$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_{k_i}$ in colour $i$ for some $i \in [r]$.
differentia: every $r$-colouring of $E(K_N)$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_{k_i}$ in colour $i$ for some $i \in [r]$
nodes.statement_short: Plan: find a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book with $t=\varepsilon k$ and $m \ge R_r(k,\dots,k,k-t)$; defines off-diagonal $R_r(k_1,\dots,k_r)$.

nodes.name: Book suffices via the multinomial bound
nodes.statement: Since we have $$R_r(k,\ldots,k,k-t) \leqslant {kr - t \choose k,\ldots,k,k-t} \leqslant e^{-t^2/6k} r^{rk-t},$$ by the method of Erd\H{o}s and Szekeres~\cite{ESz35}, this will suffice to prove Theorem~\ref{thm:Ramsey:multicolour}.
nodes.statement_short: Since $R_r(k,\dots,k,k-t) \le e^{-t^2/6k} r^{rk-t}$ (Erdős–Szekeres), such a book gives Theorem 1.1.

nodes.name: Colour-$i$ neighbourhood
nodes.statement: We will find a set $T \subset X$ of size $t = \varepsilon k$ such that $T$ induces a monochromatic clique in some colour $i \in [r]$, and $$\bigg| \bigcap_{u \in T} N_i(u) \cap Y_i \bigg| \geqslant m,$$ where we write $N_i(u)$ to denote the neighbourhood of $u$ in colour $i$.

nodes.name: Minimum relative colour-$i$ degree $p_i(X,Y)$
nodes.statement: Given sets $X,Y \subset V(K_n)$ and a colour $i \in [r]$, define $$p_i(X,Y) = \min\bigg\{ \frac{|N_i(x) \cap Y|}{|Y|} : x \in X \bigg\},$$ and note that $p_i(X',Y) \geqslant p_i(X,Y)$ for every subset $X' \subset X$.
nodes.statement_short: $p_i(X,Y)$ is the minimum over $x\in X$ of the fraction of $Y$ in the colour-$i$ neighbourhood of $x$; monotone under shrinking $X$.

nodes.name: Key lemma
nodes.statement: Let\/ $\chi$ be an\/ $r$-colouring of\/ $E(K_n)$, let\/ $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_r \subset V(K_n)$ be non-empty sets of vertices, and let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r > 0$. There exists a vertex $x \in X$, a colour $\ell \in [r]$, sets $X' \subset X$ and\/ $Y'_1,\ldots,Y'_r\,$ with\/ $Y'_i \subset N_i(x) \cap Y_i\,$ for each $i \in [r]$, and\/ $\lambda \geqslant -1$, such that \begin{equation} |X'| \geqslant \beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} |X| \qquad \text{and} \qquad p_\ell( X', Y'_\ell ) \geqslant p_\ell(X,Y_\ell) + \lambda \alpha_\ell, \end{equation} and moreover \begin{equation} |Y'_i| = p_i(X,Y_i) |Y_i| \qquad \text{and} \qquad p_i( X', Y'_i ) \geqslant p_i(X,Y_i) - \alpha_i \end{equation} for every $i \in [r]$.
assumptions: Let\/ $\chi$ be an\/ $r$-colouring of\/ $E(K_n)$, let\/ $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_r \subset V(K_n)$ be non-empty sets of vertices, and let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r > 0$
conclusions: There exists a vertex $x \in X$, a colour $\ell \in [r]$, sets $X' \subset X$ and\/ $Y'_1,\ldots,Y'_r\,$ with\/ $Y'_i \subset N_i(x) \cap Y_i\,$ for each $i \in [r]$, and\/ $\lambda \geqslant -1$, such that
|X'| \geqslant \beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} |X| \qquad \text{and} \qquad p_\ell( X', Y'_\ell ) \geqslant p_\ell(X,Y_\ell) + \lambda \alpha_\ell
nodes.statement_short: One can find $x$, colour $\ell$, $X'$ of size $\beta e^{-C\sqrt{\lambda+1}}|X|$ and $Y'_i \subset N_i(x)\cap Y_i$ boosting density in colour $\ell$ by $\lambda\alpha_\ell$ while losing at most $\alpha_i$ elsewhere.
nodes.label: key:lemma

nodes.name: Key lemma: size of $X'$ and density boost in colour $\ell$
nodes.statement: |X'| \geqslant \beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} |X| \qquad \text{and} \qquad p_\ell( X', Y'_\ell ) \geqslant p_\ell(X,Y_\ell) + \lambda \alpha_\ell,
nodes.label: eq:key:ell

nodes.name: Key lemma: sizes of $Y'_i$ and density loss
nodes.statement: |Y'_i| = p_i(X,Y_i) |Y_i| \qquad \text{and} \qquad p_i( X', Y'_i ) \geqslant p_i(X,Y_i) - \alpha_i
nodes.label: eq:key:alli

nodes.name: Book theorem
nodes.statement: Let\/ $\chi$ be an\/ $r$-colouring of\/ $E(K_n)$, and let\/ $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_r \subset V(K_n)$. For every $p > 0$ and $\mu \geqslant 2^{10} r^3$, and every $t,m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $t \geqslant \mu^5 / p^2$, the following holds. If $$|N_i(x) \cap Y_i| \geqslant p|Y_i|$$ for every $x \in X$ and $i \in [r]$, and moreover $$|X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t} \qquad \text{and} \qquad |Y_i| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m,$$ then $\chi$ contains a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book.
assumptions: Let\/ $\chi$ be an\/ $r$-colouring of\/ $E(K_n)$, and let\/ $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_r \subset V(K_n)$
every $p > 0$ and $\mu \geqslant 2^{10} r^3$, and every $t,m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $t \geqslant \mu^5 / p^2$
nodes.statement_short: If every $x\in X$ has colour-$i$ density at least $p$ into $Y_i$ and $X$, $Y_i$ are large enough, there is a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book.
nodes.label: thm:book

nodes.name: Multicolour book algorithm
nodes.statement: Set $T_1 = \cdots = T_r = \emptyset$, and repeat the following steps until either $X = \emptyset$ or $\max\big\{ |T_i| : i \in [r] \big\} = t$. \begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*., ref=\arabic*] \item Applying the key lemma: let the vertex $x \in X$, the colour $\ell \in [r]$, the sets $X' \subset X$ and $Y'_1,\ldots,Y'_r$, and $\lambda \geqslant -1$ be given by Lemma~\ref{key:lemma}, applied with \begin{equation} \alpha_i = \frac{p_i(X,Y_i) - p_0 + \delta}{t} \end{equation} for each $i \in [r]$, and go to Step~2.\smallskip \item Colour step: If $\lambda \leqslant \lambda_0$, then choose a colour $j \in [r]$ such that the set $$X'' = N_j(x) \cap X'$$ has at least $(|X'| - 1)/r$ elements, and update the sets as follows: $$X \rightarrow X'', \qquad Y_j \rightarrow Y'_j \qquad \text{and} \qquad T_j \rightarrow T_j \cup \{x\}$$ and go to Step~1. Otherwise go to Step~3.\smallskip \item Density-boost step: If $\lambda > \lambda_0$, then we update the sets as follows: $$X \rightarrow X' \qquad \text{and} \qquad Y_\ell \rightarrow Y'_\ell,$$ and go to Step~1. \end{enumerate}
input: parameters $t \in \mathbb{N}$ (the size of the book that we are trying to build), $\lambda_0 \geqslant -1$ (the cut-off between values of $\lambda$ that are `small' and `large'), and $\delta > 0$ (a small constant that bounds the total decrease in $p_i(X,Y_i)$)
nodes.statement_short: Repeatedly apply the key lemma and take a colour step (add $x$ to some $T_j$) if $\lambda \le \lambda_0$, else a density-boost step, until some $T_i$ has size $t$.

nodes.name: Choice of $\alpha_i$
nodes.statement: \alpha_i = \frac{p_i(X,Y_i) - p_0 + \delta}{t}
nodes.label: def:alpha

nodes.name: Initialise cliques
nodes.statement: Set $T_1 = \cdots = T_r = \emptyset$
nodes.statement_short: Start with empty cliques $T_1,\dots,T_r$.

nodes.name: Main loop
nodes.statement: repeat the following steps until either $X = \emptyset$ or $\max\big\{ |T_i| : i \in [r] \big\} = t$. \begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*., ref=\arabic*] \item Applying the key lemma: let the vertex $x \in X$, the colour $\ell \in [r]$, the sets $X' \subset X$ and $Y'_1,\ldots,Y'_r$, and $\lambda \geqslant -1$ be given by Lemma~\ref{key:lemma}, applied with \begin{equation} \alpha_i = \frac{p_i(X,Y_i) - p_0 + \delta}{t} \end{equation} for each $i \in [r]$, and go to Step~2.\smallskip \item Colour step: If $\lambda \leqslant \lambda_0$, then choose a colour $j \in [r]$ such that the set $$X'' = N_j(x) \cap X'$$ has at least $(|X'| - 1)/r$ elements, and update the sets as follows: $$X \rightarrow X'', \qquad Y_j \rightarrow Y'_j \qquad \text{and} \qquad T_j \rightarrow T_j \cup \{x\}$$ and go to Step~1. Otherwise go to Step~3.\smallskip \item Density-boost step: If $\lambda > \lambda_0$, then we update the sets as follows: $$X \rightarrow X' \qquad \text{and} \qquad Y_\ell \rightarrow Y'_\ell,$$ and go to Step~1. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Repeat until $X$ is empty or some $T_i$ reaches size $t$.

nodes.name: Step 1: apply the key lemma
nodes.statement: Applying the key lemma: let the vertex $x \in X$, the colour $\ell \in [r]$, the sets $X' \subset X$ and $Y'_1,\ldots,Y'_r$, and $\lambda \geqslant -1$ be given by Lemma~\ref{key:lemma}, applied with \begin{equation} \alpha_i = \frac{p_i(X,Y_i) - p_0 + \delta}{t} \end{equation} for each $i \in [r]$, and go to Step~2.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the key lemma with $\alpha_i = (p_i(X,Y_i)-p_0+\delta)/t$.

nodes.name: Step 2: colour step
nodes.statement: Colour step: If $\lambda \leqslant \lambda_0$, then choose a colour $j \in [r]$ such that the set $$X'' = N_j(x) \cap X'$$ has at least $(|X'| - 1)/r$ elements, and update the sets as follows: $$X \rightarrow X'', \qquad Y_j \rightarrow Y'_j \qquad \text{and} \qquad T_j \rightarrow T_j \cup \{x\}$$ and go to Step~1. Otherwise go to Step~3.
nodes.statement_short: If $\lambda \le \lambda_0$, pick colour $j$ with large $N_j(x)\cap X'$ and add $x$ to $T_j$.

nodes.name: Step 3: density-boost step
nodes.statement: Density-boost step: If $\lambda > \lambda_0$, then we update the sets as follows: $$X \rightarrow X' \qquad \text{and} \qquad Y_\ell \rightarrow Y'_\ell,$$ and go to Step~1.
nodes.statement_short: If $\lambda > \lambda_0$, replace $X$ by $X'$ and $Y_\ell$ by $Y'_\ell$.

nodes.name: Geometric lemma
nodes.statement: Let\/ $U$ and\/ $U'$ be i.i.d.~random variables taking values in a finite set~$X$, and let $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r \colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n$ be arbitrary functions. There exist $\lambda \geqslant -1$ and\/ $i \in [r]$ such that $$\mathbb{P}\Big( \big\langle \sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U') \big\rangle \geqslant \lambda \, \text{ and } \, \big\langle \sigma_j(U), \sigma_j(U') \big\rangle \geqslant -1 \, \text{ for all } \, j \ne i \Big) \geqslant \beta e^{- C\sqrt{\lambda + 1}}.$$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
assumptions: Let\/ $U$ and\/ $U'$ be i.i.d.~random variables taking values in a finite set~$X$, and let $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r \colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n$ be arbitrary functions
nodes.statement_short: For any maps $\sigma_i: X\to\mathbb{R}^n$, with probability $\ge \beta e^{-C\sqrt{\lambda+1}}$ one inner product is $\ge\lambda$ and all others $\ge -1$.
nodes.label: lem:lambda

nodes.name: Proof idea for the geometric lemma
nodes.statement: The idea of the proof is as follows. We will first observe (see Lemma~\ref{lem:moments}) that all of the moments of the inner products $\langle \sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U') \rangle$ are positive. The key step is then to define a function $f \colon \mathbb{R}^r \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ (see~\eqref{def:f}) whose Taylor expansion has non-negative coefficients, that is only positive close to the positive quadrant, and that does not grow too fast. With this function in hand, the lemma will then follow from a simple calculation.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: moments of inner products are non-negative; a special function with non-negative Taylor coefficients then forces the bound.

nodes.name: Standard inner product notation
nodes.statement: In this section we will write $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ to denote the standard inner product on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Non-negativity of mixed moments of inner products
nodes.statement: Let $U$ and\/ $U'$ be i.i.d.~random variables taking values in a finite set~$X$, and let\/ $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r \colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n$ be arbitrary functions. Then $$\mathbb{E}\Big[ \big\langle \sigma_1(U),\sigma_1(U') \big\rangle^{\ell_1} \cdots \big\langle \sigma_r(U),\sigma_r(U') \big\rangle^{\ell_r} \Big] \geqslant 0$$ for every $(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r) \in \mathbb{Z}^r$ with $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r \geqslant 0$.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
assumptions: Let $U$ and\/ $U'$ be i.i.d.~random variables taking values in a finite set~$X$, and let\/ $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r \colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n$ be arbitrary functions
nodes.statement_short: All mixed moments of the inner products $\langle\sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U')\rangle$ are non-negative.
nodes.label: lem:moments

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: To simplify the notation, let us write $$\big\langle \sigma_1(U),\sigma_1(U') \big\rangle^{\ell_1} \cdots \big\langle \sigma_r(U), \sigma_r(U') \big\rangle^{\ell_r} = \prod_{i = 1}^\ell \big\langle \sigma_{a_i}(U), \sigma_{a_i}(U') \big\rangle $$ where $\ell = \ell_1 + \cdots + \ell_r$ and $(a_1,\dots,a_\ell)$ is such that $\big| \big\{ i \in [\ell] : a_i = j \big\} \big| = \ell_j$ for each $j \in [r]$. Now set $$Z = \sigma_{a_1}(U) \otimes \sigma_{a_2}(U) \otimes \cdots \otimes \sigma_{a_\ell}(U) \quad \text{and} \quad Z' = \sigma_{a_1}(U') \otimes \sigma_{a_2}(U') \otimes \cdots \otimes \sigma_{a_\ell}(U'),$$ and note that $$\big\langle Z, Z' \big\rangle = \prod_{i = 1}^\ell \big\langle \sigma_{a_i}(U), \sigma_{a_i}(U') \big\rangle,$$ since $\langle u_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes u_r, v_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes v_r \rangle = \langle u_1, v_1 \rangle \cdots \langle v_r , u_r \rangle $ for any vectors $u_i,v_i \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Finally, note that $Z$ and $Z'$ are independent and identically distributed random vectors, and therefore $$\mathbb{E} \big[ \langle Z, Z' \rangle \big] = \mathbb{E}_{Z'} \big[ \mathbb{E}_Z \big[ \langle Z, Z' \rangle \big] \big] = \mathbb{E}_{Z'} \big[ \big\langle \mathbb{E}[Z], Z' \big\rangle \big] = \big\langle \mathbb{E}[Z], \mathbb{E}[Z'] \big\rangle \geqslant 0,$$ as required, where the final inequality holds because $\mathbb{E}[Z] = \mathbb{E}[Z']$.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Write the product of inner products as one inner product of tensor powers; for i.i.d. vectors $\mathbb{E}\langle Z,Z'\rangle = |\mathbb{E}Z|^2 \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Special function $f$
nodes.statement: Next, we will need the following special function: \begin{equation} f(x_1,\dots,x_r) = \sum_{j = 1}^r x_j \prod_{i \ne j} \big( 2 + \cosh\sqrt{x_i} \big), \end{equation} where we define $\cosh \sqrt{x}$ via its Taylor expansion $$\cosh\sqrt{x} = \sum_{n = 0}^\infty \frac{x^n}{(2n)!}.$$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.statement_short: $f(x)=\sum_j x_j\prod_{i\ne j}(2+\cosh\sqrt{x_i})$, with $\cosh\sqrt{x}$ defined by its Taylor series.

nodes.name: Definition of the special function $f$
nodes.statement: f(x_1,\dots,x_r) = \sum_{j = 1}^r x_j \prod_{i \ne j} \big( 2 + \cosh\sqrt{x_i} \big),
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.label: def:f

nodes.name: Taylor coefficients of $f$ are non-negative
nodes.statement: In particular, note that all of the coefficients of the Taylor expansion of $f$ are non-negative.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
conclusions: all of the coefficients of the Taylor expansion of $f$ are non-negative

nodes.name: Growth bounds for the special function
nodes.statement: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. The function $f \colon \mathbb{R}^r \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ defined in~\eqref{def:f} satisfies $$ f(x_1,\dots,x_r) \leqslant \left\{\begin{array}{cl} 3^r r \exp\bigg( \displaystyle\sum_{i = 1}^r \sqrt{ x_i + 3r } \bigg) \quad & \text{if } \,\, x_i \geqslant - 3r \,\text{ for all }\, i \in [r];\\[+3ex] -1 & \text{otherwise.} \end{array} \right. $$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.statement_short: $f \le 3^r r\exp(\sum_i\sqrt{x_i+3r})$ when all $x_i \ge -3r$, and $f \le -1$ otherwise.
nodes.label: lem:special:function

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: Observe first that $x \leqslant 2 + \cosh\sqrt{x} \leqslant 3e^{\sqrt{x}}$ for every $x \geqslant 0$, that $$f(x_1,\dots,x_r) = \bigg( \prod_{i = 1}^r \big( 2 + \cosh \sqrt{x_i} \big) \bigg) \sum_{j = 1}^r \frac{x_j}{2+\cosh\sqrt{x_j}},$$ and that $\cosh \sqrt{x} = \cos \sqrt{-x}$, and hence $-1 \leqslant \cosh \sqrt{x} \leqslant 1$ for all $x < 0$. It follows that \begin{equation} 1 \leqslant 2 + \cosh\sqrt{x} \leqslant 3e^{\sqrt{x+3r}} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \frac{x}{2+\cosh\sqrt{x}} \leqslant 1 \end{equation} for all $x \geqslant -3r$, and hence $$f(x_1,\dots,x_r)\leqslant r \prod_{i=1}^r 3e^{\sqrt{x_i + 3r}} = 3^r r \exp\bigg(\sum_{i=1}^r \sqrt{x_i + 3r} \bigg),$$ for every $x_1,\ldots,x_r \geqslant -3r$, as claimed. Moreover, if $x_i \leqslant -3r$, then, again using~\eqref{eq:cosh:bounds}, $$\sum_{j = 1}^r \frac{x_j}{2+\cosh\sqrt{x_j}} \leqslant \frac{x_i}{3} + r - 1 \leqslant - 1.$$ Since $2 + \cosh \sqrt{x} \geqslant 1$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, it follows that $f(x_1,\dots,x_r) \leqslant -1$, as required.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Bound each factor $2+\cosh\sqrt{x}$ using $\cosh\sqrt{x}=\cos\sqrt{-x}$ for $x<0$; treat the cases all $x_i\ge-3r$ and some $x_i\le -3r$.

nodes.name: Bounds on $2+\cosh\sqrt{x}$
nodes.statement: 1 \leqslant 2 + \cosh\sqrt{x} \leqslant 3e^{\sqrt{x+3r}} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \frac{x}{2+\cosh\sqrt{x}} \leqslant 1
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.label: eq:cosh:bounds

nodes.name: Optimality of the growth of $f$ (Phragmén–Lindelöf)
nodes.statement: The key idea in the lemma above was to find an entire function, $2 + \cosh\sqrt{x}$, which $(a)$ has a Taylor expansion at $x = 0$ with non-negative coefficients; $(b)$ is bounded on the negative real axis; and $(c)$ does not grow too quickly on the positive axis. The Phragm\'en--Lindel\"of theorem implies that functions satisfying $(a)$ and $(b)$ must grow at least as fast as $\exp\big( x^{1/2+o(1)} \big)$ on the positive real axis. Thus the bound on the growth of $f$ given by the lemma is essentially best possible for constructions of this type.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.statement_short: By Phragmén–Lindelöf, functions with non-negative Taylor coefficients bounded on the negative axis grow like $\exp(x^{1/2+o(1)})$, so the bound is essentially optimal.

nodes.name: Proof of the geometric lemma
nodes.statement: For each $i \in [r]$, define $Z_i = 3r\big\langle \sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U') \big\rangle$, and observe that, by Lemma~\ref{lem:moments} and linearity of expectation, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\big[ f\big( Z_1,\ldots,Z_r \big) \big] \geqslant 0, \end{equation} since all of the coefficients of the Taylor expansion of $f$ are non-negative. By Lemma~\ref{lem:special:function}, it follows that if we define $E$ to be the event that $Z_i \geqslant -3r$ for every $i \in [r]$, then \begin{equation} 3^r r \cdot \mathbb{E}\bigg[ \exp\bigg( \sum_{i = 1}^r \sqrt{ Z_i + 3r } \bigg) \mathbf{1}_E \bigg] \geqslant 1 - \mathbb{P}(E), \end{equation} where $\mathbf{1}_E \in \{0,1\}$ denotes the indicator of the event $E$, since the left-hand side bounds the contribution to the expectation on the left-hand side of~\eqref{eq:Ex:f:positive} due to the event $E$, and the right-hand side bounds the contribution to the expectation due to the event $E^c$. The result now follows from a simple calculation. First, note that $$\mathbb{P}(E) = \mathbb{P}\Big( Z_i \geqslant - 3r \, \text{ for all } \, i \in [r] \Big),$$ so if $\mathbb{P}(E) \geqslant \beta$, then the claimed inequality holds with $\lambda = -1$. We claim that if $\mathbb{P}(E) \leqslant \beta$, then there exists $\lambda \geqslant -1$ such that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \geqslant \beta r e^{-C\sqrt{\lambda + 1}}, \end{equation} where $M = \max \big\{ \big\langle \sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U') \big\rangle : i \in [r] \big\}$, and therefore (by the union bound) there exists an $i \in [r]$ as required. To see this, set $f(x) = e^{c \sqrt{x + 1}}$ with $c = \sqrt{3}r^{3/2}$, and observe that $$\mathbb{E}\big[ f(M) \mathbf{1}_E \big] \, \leqslant \, \mathbb{P}(E) + \int_{-1}^\infty \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \cdot f'(\lambda) \,\mathrm{d}\lambda$$ since $f(-1) = 1$ and if $E$ holds then $M \geqslant -1$. It follows that if $\mathbb{P}(E) \leqslant \beta$ and~\eqref{eq:max:big:and:E} does not hold for any $\lambda \geqslant -1$, then \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[ \exp\big( c \sqrt{M + 1} \big) \mathbf{1}_E \Big] & \leqslant \, \mathbb{P}(E) + \int_{-1}^\infty \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \cdot \frac{c}{2\sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \cdot e^{c \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \,\mathrm{d}\lambda\\ & \leqslant \, \beta + \beta r \int_{-1}^\infty \frac{c}{2\sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \cdot e^{- \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \,\mathrm{d}\lambda \, \leqslant \, \beta (cr + 1), \end{align*} where in the second step we used our choice of $C = 4r^{3/2} \geqslant c + 1$, and in the final step we used the fact that $\int_0^\infty \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} e^{-\sqrt{x}} \, \mathrm{d}x = 1$. In particular, recalling that $\beta = 3^{-4r}$, it follows that the left-hand side of~\eqref{eq:eventE:inequality} is at most $3^r r \cdot 3^{-4r} \big( \sqrt{3}r^{5/2} + 1 \big) \leqslant 1/2$, which contradicts our assumption that $\mathbb{P}(E) \leqslant \beta$. Hence there exists $\lambda \geqslant -1$ such that~\eqref{eq:max:big:and:E} holds, as claimed.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Apply $f$ to $Z_i = 3r\langle\sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U')\rangle$: $\mathbb{E} f \ge 0$ by Lemma 3.2, then compare contributions on $E$ and $E^c$. If $\mathbb{P}(E)\le\beta$, integrating tails of $e^{c\sqrt{M+1}}$ yields a contradiction unless (9) holds.

nodes.name: $\mathbb{E} f(Z) \ge 0$
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\big[ f\big( Z_1,\ldots,Z_r \big) \big] \geqslant 0,
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.label: eq:Ex:f:positive

nodes.name: Contribution of the event $E$
nodes.statement: 3^r r \cdot \mathbb{E}\bigg[ \exp\bigg( \sum_{i = 1}^r \sqrt{ Z_i + 3r } \bigg) \mathbf{1}_E \bigg] \geqslant 1 - \mathbb{P}(E),
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.label: eq:eventE:inequality

nodes.name: Tail bound for the maximum inner product
nodes.statement: \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \geqslant \beta r e^{-C\sqrt{\lambda + 1}},
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.label: eq:max:big:and:E

nodes.name: Proof of the key lemma
nodes.statement: For each colour $i \in [r]$, define a function $\sigma_i \colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{Y_i}$ as follows: for each $x \in X$, choose a set $N'_i(x) \subset N_i(x) \cap Y_i$ of size exactly $p_i|Y_i|$, where $p_i = p_i(X,Y_i)$, and set $$\sigma_i(x) = \frac{\hbox{$1\mkern-6.5mu1$}_{N'_i(x)} - p_i\hbox{$1\mkern-6.5mu1$}_{Y_i}}{\sqrt{\alpha_ip_i|Y_i|}},$$ where $\hbox{$1\mkern-6.5mu1$}_S \in \{0,1\}^{Y_i}$ denotes the indicator function of the set $S$. Note that, for any $x,y\in X$, $$\big\langle \sigma_i(x),\sigma_i(y) \big\rangle \geqslant \lambda \quad \Leftrightarrow \quad |N'_i(x) \cap N'_i(y)|\geqslant \big( p_i + \lambda\alpha_i \big) p_i |Y_i|.$$ Now, by Lemma~\ref{lem:lambda}, there exists $\lambda \geqslant -1$ and a colour $\ell \in [r]$ such that $$\mathbb{P}\Big( \big\langle \sigma_\ell(U),\sigma_\ell(U') \big\rangle \geqslant \lambda \, \text{ and } \, \big\langle \sigma_i(U), \sigma_i(U') \big\rangle \geqslant -1 \, \text{ for all } \, i \ne \ell \Big) \geqslant \beta e^{- C\sqrt{\lambda + 1}}.$$ where $U$, $U'$ are independent random variables distributed uniformly in the set~$X$. Hence there exists a vertex $x \in X$ and a set $X' \subset X$ such that, $$|X'| \geqslant \beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} |X| \qquad \text{and} \qquad |N'_\ell(x) \cap N'_\ell(y)| \geqslant \big( p_\ell + \lambda\alpha_\ell \big) p_\ell |Y_\ell |$$ for every $y \in X'$, and $$|N'_i(x) \cap N'_i(y)|\geqslant \big( p_i - \alpha_i \big) p_i |Y_i|$$ for every $y \in X'$ and $i \in [r]$. Setting $Y'_i = N'_i(x)$ for each $i \in [r]$, it follows that $$p_\ell\big( X', Y'_\ell \big) \geqslant p_\ell(X,Y_\ell) + \lambda \alpha_\ell \qquad \text{and} \qquad p_i\big( X', Y'_i \big) \geqslant p_i(X,Y_i) - \alpha_i$$ for every $i \in [r]$, as required.
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma
nodes.statement_short: Encode colour-$i$ neighbourhoods as centred normalised vectors $\sigma_i(x)$ and apply the geometric lemma to uniform $U,U'$ on $X$.

nodes.name: Initial minimum density $p_0$
nodes.statement: Define \begin{equation} p_0 = \min\big\{ p_i(X,Y_i) : i \in [r] \big\}, \end{equation} and run the algorithm for some $t \in \mathbb{N}$, $\lambda_0 \geqslant 0$ and $\delta > 0$.
also_stated_at: We also set $$p_0 = \min\big\{ p_i(X,Y_i) : i \in [r] \big\},$$ and emphasize that $t$, $\lambda_0$, $\delta$ and $p_0$ remain fixed throughout the algorithm.

nodes.name: Definition of $p_0$
nodes.statement: p_0 = \min\big\{ p_i(X,Y_i) : i \in [r] \big\},
nodes.label: def:p0

nodes.name: Sets and densities after $s$ steps
nodes.statement: In order to simplify the statements of the lemmas below, let us write $X(s)$ and $Y_i(s)$ for the sets $X$ and $Y_i$ after $s$ steps of the algorithm, and set $$p_i(s) = p_i\big( X(s), Y_i(s) \big) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \alpha_i(s) = \frac{p_i(s) - p_0 + \delta}{t}.$$

nodes.name: Density-boost steps $\mathcal{B}_i(s)$
nodes.statement: Let us also write $\ell(s) \in [r]$ and $\lambda(s) \geqslant -1$ for the colour and number given by the application of Lemma~\ref{key:lemma} to the sets $X(s)$ and $Y_1(s),\dots,Y_r(s)$, and define $$\mathcal{B}_i(s) = \big\{ 0 \leqslant j < s \,:\, \ell(j) = i \, \text{ and } \, \lambda(j) > \lambda_0 \big\},$$ for each $i \in [r]$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$, to be the set of density-boost steps in colour $i$ during the first $s$ steps of the algorithm.
nodes.statement_short: $\ell(s),\lambda(s)$ are the key-lemma outputs at step $s$; $\mathcal{B}_i(s)$ is the set of density-boost steps in colour $i$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $p_i(s)$
nodes.statement: For each $i \in [r]$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$, \begin{equation} p_i(s) - p_0 + \delta \, \geqslant \, \delta \cdot \bigg( 1 - \frac{1}{t} \bigg)^{t} \prod_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(j)}{t} \bigg). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $p_i(s)-p_0+\delta$ loses at most a factor $(1-1/t)$ per colour step and gains $(1+\lambda/t)$ per density-boost step.
nodes.label: lem:pi:lower:bound

nodes.name: Lower bound on $p_i(s) - p_0 + \delta$
nodes.statement: p_i(s) - p_0 + \delta \, \geqslant \, \delta \cdot \bigg( 1 - \frac{1}{t} \bigg)^{t} \prod_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(j)}{t} \bigg).
nodes.label: eq:pi:lower:bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Note first that if $Y_i(s+1) = Y_i(s)$, then $p_i(s+1) \geqslant p_i(s)$, since the minimum degree does not decrease when we take a subset of $X(s)$. When we perform a colour step in colour $i$, we have $p_i(s+1) \geqslant p_i(s) - \alpha_i(s)$, by Lemma~\ref{key:lemma}, and hence $$p_i(s+1) - p_0 + \delta \geqslant \bigg( 1 - \frac{1}{t} \bigg) \big( p_i(s) - p_0 + \delta \big),$$ by our choice of $\alpha_i(s)$. Similarly, when we perform a density-boost step in colour $i$ we have $p_i(s+1) \geqslant p_i(s) + \lambda(s) \alpha_i(s)$, by Lemma~\ref{key:lemma}, and hence $$p_i(s+1) - p_0 + \delta \geqslant \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(s)}{t} \bigg) \big( p_i(s) - p_0 + \delta \big).$$ Recalling that there are at most $t$ colour steps in colour $i$, and that $p_i(0) \geqslant p_0$, by the definition~\eqref{def:p0} of $p_0$, the claimed bound follows.
nodes.statement_short: Track $p_i(s)-p_0+\delta$ step by step via the key lemma: unchanged, multiplied by $(1-1/t)$, or by $(1+\lambda/t)$.

nodes.name: $p_i(s)$ and $\alpha_i(s)$ stay large
nodes.statement: If\/ $t \geqslant 2$, then $$p_i(s) \, \geqslant \, p_0 - \frac{3\delta}{4} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \alpha_i(s) \, \geqslant \, \frac{\delta}{4t}$$ for every $i \in [r]$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.label: lem:pi:min

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: Both bounds follow immediately from~\eqref{eq:pi:lower:bound} and the definition of $\alpha_i(s)$, since we chose $\lambda_0 \geqslant 0$ and using the fact that $( 1 - 1/t )^t \geqslant 1/4$ for every $t \geqslant 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from (11) using $(1-1/t)^t \ge 1/4$.

nodes.name: Few density-boost steps
nodes.statement: If\/ $t \geqslant \lambda_0 \geqslant 2$ and\/ $\delta \leqslant 1/4$, then $$|\mathcal{B}_i(s)| \leqslant \frac{4 \log(1/\delta)}{\lambda_0} \cdot t$$ for every $i \in [r]$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.label: lem:Bi:max

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: Since $\lambda(j) > \lambda_0$ for every $j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)$, and $p_i(s) \leqslant 1$, it follows from~\eqref{eq:pi:lower:bound} that $$\frac{\delta}{4} \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda_0}{t} \bigg)^{|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} \leqslant 1 + \delta.$$ Since $t \geqslant \lambda_0$ and $\delta \leqslant 1/4$, the claimed bound follows.
nodes.statement_short: Since $p_i(s)\le1$, (11) gives $(\delta/4)(1+\lambda_0/t)^{|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} \le 1+\delta$; solve for $|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $|Y_i(s)|$
nodes.statement: If\/ $t \geqslant 2$, then $$|Y_i(s)| \geqslant \bigg( p_0 - \frac{3\delta}{4} \bigg)^{t + |\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} |Y_i(0)|$$ for every $i \in [r]$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.label: lem:Y:lower:bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: Note that $Y_i(j+1) \ne Y_i(j)$ for at most $t + |\mathcal{B}_i(s)|$ of the first $s$ steps, and for those steps we have $$|Y_i(j+1)| = p_i(j) |Y_i(j)| \geqslant \bigg( p_0 - \frac{3\delta}{4} \bigg) |Y_i(j)|,$$ by~\eqref{eq:key:alli} and Lemma~\ref{lem:pi:min}.
nodes.statement_short: $Y_i$ changes in at most $t+|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|$ steps, each time shrinking by a factor $p_i(j) \ge p_0-3\delta/4$.

nodes.name: $\varepsilon$ and the set $\mathcal{B}(s)$ of all density-boost steps
nodes.statement: To do so, set $\varepsilon = (\beta / r) e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda_0 + 1}}$, and define $\mathcal{B}(s) = \mathcal{B}_1(s) \cup \cdots \cup \mathcal{B}_r(s)$ to be the set of all density-boost steps.

nodes.name: Lower bound on $|X(s)|$
nodes.statement: For each $s \in \mathbb{N}$, \begin{equation} |X(s)| \geqslant \varepsilon^{rt + |\mathcal{B}(s)|} \exp\bigg( - C \sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}(s)} \sqrt{\lambda(j)+1}\,\, \bigg) |X(0)| - rt. \end{equation}
nodes.label: lem:X:lower:bound

nodes.name: Lower bound on $|X(s)|$
nodes.statement: |X(s)| \geqslant \varepsilon^{rt + |\mathcal{B}(s)|} \exp\bigg( - C \sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}(s)} \sqrt{\lambda(j)+1}\,\, \bigg) |X(0)| - rt.
nodes.label: eq:X:lower:bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement: If $\lambda(j) \leqslant \lambda_0$, then by~\eqref{eq:key:ell} and Step~2 of the algorithm we have $$|X(j+1)| \geqslant \frac{\beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda_0 + 1}}}{r} \cdot |X(j)| - 1 = \varepsilon |X(j)| - 1.$$ On the other hand, if $\lambda(j) > \lambda_0$, then $j \in \mathcal{B}(s)$, and we have $$|X(j+1)| \geqslant \beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda(j) + 1}} |X(j)|,$$ by~\eqref{eq:key:ell} and Step~3 of the algorithm. Since there are at most $rt$ colour steps, and $\beta \geqslant \varepsilon$, the claimed bound follows.
nodes.statement_short: Colour steps shrink $X$ by a factor $\varepsilon$ (minus 1), density-boost steps by $\beta e^{-C\sqrt{\lambda+1}}$; at most $rt$ colour steps.

nodes.name: Bound on the sum of the $\sqrt{\lambda}$
nodes.statement: If\/ $t \geqslant \lambda_0 / \delta > 0$ and\/ $\delta \leqslant 1/4$, then $$\sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}(s)} \sqrt{\lambda(j)} \leqslant \frac{7r \log(1/\delta)}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}} \cdot t$$ for every $s \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.label: lem:sum:of:lambdas

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement: Observe first that, by Lemma~\ref{lem:pi:lower:bound}, we have \begin{equation} \frac{\delta}{4} \prod_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(j)}{t} \bigg) \leqslant 1 + \delta \end{equation} for each $i \in [r]$. Note also that $\lambda_0 \leqslant \lambda(j) \leqslant 5t/\delta$ for every $j \in \mathcal{B}(s)$, where the lower bound holds by the definition of $\mathcal{B}(s)$, and the upper bound by~\eqref{eq:B:condition} and since $\delta \leqslant 1/4$. Now, since $\log(1+x) \geqslant \min\{ x/2,1\}$ for all $x > 0$, it follows that \begin{equation} \frac{ \sqrt{\lambda(j)} }{\log(1 + \lambda(j)/t) } \leqslant \max\bigg\{ \frac{ 2t }{ \sqrt{\lambda_0} }, \, \sqrt{ \frac{5t}{\delta}} \bigg\} \leqslant \frac{ 3t }{ \sqrt{\lambda_0} }, \end{equation} where in the second inequality we used our assumption that $t \geqslant \lambda_0 / \delta$. It now follows that $$\sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \sqrt{\lambda(j)} \leqslant \frac{ 3t }{ \sqrt{\lambda_0} } \sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \log \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(j)}{t} \bigg) \leqslant \frac{7 \log(1/\delta)}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}} \cdot t,$$ where the first inequality holds by~\eqref{eq:not:convexity}, and the second follows from~\eqref{eq:B:condition}, since $\delta \leqslant 1/4$. Summing over $i \in [r]$, we obtain the claimed bound.
nodes.statement_short: From (13), bound each $\sqrt{\lambda(j)}$ by $(3t/\sqrt{\lambda_0})\log(1+\lambda(j)/t)$, sum the logarithms and then sum over colours.

nodes.name: Product condition on density-boost steps
nodes.statement: \frac{\delta}{4} \prod_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(j)}{t} \bigg) \leqslant 1 + \delta
nodes.label: eq:B:condition

nodes.name: Ratio bound $\sqrt{\lambda}/\log(1+\lambda/t)$
nodes.statement: \frac{ \sqrt{\lambda(j)} }{\log(1 + \lambda(j)/t) } \leqslant \max\bigg\{ \frac{ 2t }{ \sqrt{\lambda_0} }, \, \sqrt{ \frac{5t}{\delta}} \bigg\} \leqslant \frac{ 3t }{ \sqrt{\lambda_0} },
nodes.label: eq:not:convexity

nodes.name: Proof of the book theorem
nodes.statement: Recall that we are given an $r$-colouring $\chi$ of $E(K_n)$ and a collection of sets $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_r \subset V(K_n)$ with \begin{equation} |X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t} \qquad \text{and} \qquad |Y_i| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m \end{equation} for each $i \in [r]$, for some $p \in (0,1]$, $\mu \geqslant 2^{10} r^3$ and $t,m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $t \geqslant \mu^5 / p^2$, and moreover \begin{equation} |N_i(x) \cap Y_i| \geqslant p|Y_i| \end{equation} for every $x \in X$ and $i \in [r]$. We will run the multicolour book algorithm with \begin{equation} \delta = \frac{p}{\mu^2} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \lambda_0 = \bigg( \frac{\mu \log(1/\delta)}{8C} \bigg)^2, \end{equation} where $C = 4r^{3/2}$ (as before), and show that it ends with $$\max \big\{ |T_i(s)| : i \in [r] \big\} = t \qquad \text{and} \qquad \min\big\{ |Y_i(s)| : i \in [r] \big\} \geqslant m,$$ and therefore produces a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book. To do so, we just need to bound the sizes of the sets $X(s)$ and $Y_i(s)$ from below. Observe that $t \geqslant \lambda_0$ and $\delta \leqslant 1/4$, and therefore, by Lemma~\ref{lem:Bi:max}, that \begin{equation} |\mathcal{B}_i(s)| \, \leqslant \, \frac{4 \log(1/\delta)}{\lambda_0} \cdot t \, = \, \frac{2^{12} r^3}{\mu^2 \log(1/\delta)} \cdot t \, \leqslant \, t \end{equation} for every $i \in [r]$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Since $p_0 \geqslant p$, by~\eqref{eq:book:thm:min:degree} and the definition of $p_0$, it follows that $$|Y_i(s)| \, \geqslant \, \bigg( p - \frac{3\delta}{4} \bigg)^{t + |\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} |Y_i| \, \geqslant \, e^{-2\delta t / p} \, p^{|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} \, \big( e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2} \big)^t \, m,$$ where the first inequality holds by Lemma~\ref{lem:Y:lower:bound}, and the second by~\eqref{eq:book:thm:conditions} and~\eqref{eq:Bi:final:bound}. Noting that $p^{|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} \geqslant e^{-2^{12} r^3 t / \mu^2}$, by~\eqref{eq:Bi:final:bound}, and that $\delta / p = 1/\mu^2$, it follows that $$|Y_i(s)| \, \geqslant \, e^{-2 t / \mu^2} \big( e^{2^{12} r^3 / \mu^2} \big)^t \, m \, \geqslant \, m,$$ as claimed. To bound $|X(s)|$, recall~\eqref{eq:X:lower:bound} and observe that $$\varepsilon^{rt + |\mathcal{B}(s)|} \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\beta}{r} \cdot e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda_0 + 1}} \bigg)^{2rt} \geqslant \big( e^{- 4C \sqrt{\lambda_0}} \big)^{rt} = \delta^{\mu r t/2} = \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{-\mu r t / 2},$$ where the first step holds because $\varepsilon = (\beta / r) e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda_0 + 1}}$ and $|\mathcal{B}(s)| \leqslant rt$, by~\eqref{eq:Bi:final:bound}, the second step holds because $\beta = 3^{-4r}$ and $\lambda_0 \geqslant 2^{10} r^3$, and the third and fourth steps follow from our choice of $\lambda_0$ and $\delta$ in~\eqref{def:delta:lambda0}. Moreover, observe that $t \geqslant \lambda_0 / \delta$, and therefore $$\sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}(s)} \sqrt{\lambda(j)+1} \leqslant \frac{8r \log(1/\delta)}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}} \cdot t = \frac{2^6Crt}{\mu},$$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:sum:of:lambdas} and our choice of $\lambda_0$, and therefore $$|X(s)| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t / 2} \exp\bigg( - \frac{2^6C^2rt}{\mu} \bigg) - rt > 0,$$ for every $s \in \mathbb{N}$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:X:lower:bound} and since $\mu \geqslant 2^{10} r^3$ and $C = 4r^{3/2}$. It follows that the algorithm produces a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book, as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Run the multicolour book algorithm with $\delta=p/\mu^2$ and $\lambda_0=(\mu\log(1/\delta)/8C)^2$. Lemmas 4.3–4.6 keep $|Y_i(s)|\ge m$ and $|X(s)|>0$, so some $T_i$ reaches size $t$.

nodes.name: Book theorem size conditions (restated)
nodes.statement: |X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t} \qquad \text{and} \qquad |Y_i| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m
nodes.label: eq:book:thm:conditions

nodes.name: Book theorem minimum-degree condition (restated)
nodes.statement: |N_i(x) \cap Y_i| \geqslant p|Y_i|
nodes.label: eq:book:thm:min:degree

nodes.name: Choice of $\delta$ and $\lambda_0$
nodes.statement: \delta = \frac{p}{\mu^2} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \lambda_0 = \bigg( \frac{\mu \log(1/\delta)}{8C} \bigg)^2,
nodes.label: def:delta:lambda0

nodes.name: Final bound on $|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|$
nodes.statement: |\mathcal{B}_i(s)| \, \leqslant \, \frac{4 \log(1/\delta)}{\lambda_0} \cdot t \, = \, \frac{2^{12} r^3}{\mu^2 \log(1/\delta)} \cdot t \, \leqslant \, t
nodes.label: eq:Bi:final:bound

nodes.name: Deduction of Theorem 1.1 from Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement: In this section we will deduce Theorem~\ref{thm:Ramsey:multicolour}, our bound on the Ramsey numbers $R_r(k)$, from Theorem~\ref{thm:book}. We will in fact prove the following quantitative version of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.1 is deduced from the book theorem via its quantitative version, Theorem 5.1.

nodes.name: Quantitative multicolour Ramsey bound
nodes.statement: Let $r \geqslant 2$, and set $\delta = 2^{-160} r^{-12}$. Then $$R_r(k) \leqslant e^{-\delta k} r^{rk}$$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \geqslant 2^{200} r^{20}$.
nodes.statement_short: $R_r(k) \le e^{-\delta k} r^{rk}$ with $\delta = 2^{-160}r^{-12}$ for all $k \ge 2^{200}r^{20}$.
nodes.label: thm:Ramsey:multicolour:quant

nodes.name: Erdős–Szekeres steps to a near-regular set
nodes.statement: Given\/ $n,r \in \mathbb{N}$ and\/ $\varepsilon > 0$, and an $r$-colouring of $E(K_n)$, the following holds. There exist disjoint sets of vertices\/ $S_1,\dots,S_r$ and\/ $W$ such that, for every $i \in [r]$, $$|W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j|} n \qquad \text{and} \qquad |N_i(w) \cap W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1}{r} - \varepsilon \bigg) |W| - 1$$ for every $w \in W$, and $(S_i,W)$ is a monochromatic book in colour~$i$.
conclusions: There exist disjoint sets of vertices\/ $S_1,\dots,S_r$ and\/ $W$ such that, for every $i \in [r]$,
$(S_i,W)$ is a monochromatic book in colour~$i$
nodes.statement_short: Running Erdős–Szekeres steps yields books $(S_i,W)$ in each colour with $W$ large and every colour of minimum degree about $|W|/r$ inside $W$.
nodes.label: lem:ESz:steps

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: We use induction on~$n$. Note that if $n \leqslant r$ or $r = 1$, then the sets $S_1 = \cdots = S_r = \emptyset$ and $W = V(K_n)$ have the required properties. We may therefore assume that $n > r \geqslant 2$, and that there exists a vertex $x \in V(K_n)$ and a colour $\ell \in [r]$ such that $$|N_\ell(x)| < \bigg( \frac{1}{r} - \varepsilon \bigg) n - 1,$$ and hence there exists a different colour $j \ne \ell$ such that $$|N_j(x)| \geqslant \frac{1}{r-1} \bigg( n - \bigg( \frac{1}{r} - \varepsilon \bigg) n \bigg) \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1 + \varepsilon}{r} \bigg) n.$$ Applying the induction hypothesis to the colouring induced by the set $N_j(x)$, we obtain sets $S'_1,\ldots,S'_r$ and $W'$ satisfying the conclusion of the lemma with $n$ replaced by $|N_j(x)|$. Setting $$W = W', \qquad S_j = S'_j \cup \{x\} \qquad \text{and} \qquad S_i = S'_i \qquad \text{for each } \, i \ne j,$$ we see that $W$ satisfies the minimum degree condition (by the induction hypothesis), and $$|W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\sum_{i = 1}^r |S'_i|}|N_j(x)| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\sum_{i=1}^r |S_i|}n.$$ Since $(S_i,W)$ is a monochromatic book in colour~$i$ for each $i \in [r]$, it follows that $S_1,\dots,S_r$ and $W$ are sets with the claimed properties.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $n$: if some vertex has small degree in a colour, it has large degree in another colour $j$; recurse inside $N_j(x)$ and add $x$ to $S_j$.

nodes.name: Off-diagonal Ramsey bound after many Erdős–Szekeres steps
nodes.statement: If\/ $k,r \geqslant 2$ and\/ $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, then $$R_r\big( k - s_1, \ldots, k - s_r \big) \leqslant e^{-\varepsilon^3 k / 2} \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^s r^{rk}$$ for every $s_1,\ldots,s_r \in [k]$ with\/ $s = s_1 + \cdots + s_r \geqslant \varepsilon^2 k$.
assumptions: for every $s_1,\ldots,s_r \in [k]$ with\/ $s = s_1 + \cdots + s_r \geqslant \varepsilon^2 k$
conclusions: R_r\big( k - s_1, \ldots, k - s_r \big) \leqslant e^{-\varepsilon^3 k / 2} \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^s r^{rk}
nodes.label: lem:many:ESz:steps

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3
nodes.statement: By the Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres bound, we have $$R_r\big( k - s_1, \ldots, k - s_r \big) \leqslant r^{rk - s}.$$ The claimed bound follows, since $( 1 + \varepsilon )^{\varepsilon^2 k} \geqslant e^{\varepsilon^3 k/2}$ for every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Erdős–Szekeres gives $r^{rk-s}$; then use $(1+\varepsilon)^{\varepsilon^2 k} \ge e^{\varepsilon^3 k/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement: Given $r \geqslant 2$, set $\delta = 2^{-160} r^{-12}$, let $k \geqslant 2^{200} r^{20}$ and $n \geqslant e^{-\delta k} r^{rk}$, and let $\chi$ be an arbitrary $r$-colouring of $E(K_n)$. Set $\varepsilon = 2^{-50} r^{-4}$, and let $S_1,\ldots,S_r$ and $W$ be the sets given by Lemma~\ref{lem:ESz:steps}. Suppose first that $|S_1| + \cdots + |S_r| \geqslant \varepsilon^2 k$, and observe that, by Lemma~\ref{lem:many:ESz:steps} and our lower bounds on $n$ and $|W|$, we have $$|W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j|} e^{-\delta k} r^{rk} \geqslant R_r\big( k - |S_1|, \ldots, k - |S_r| \big).$$ Since $(S_i,W)$ is a monochromatic book in colour~$i$ for each $i \in [r]$, it follows that there exists a monochromatic copy of $K_k$ in $\chi$, as required. We may therefore assume from now on that $|S_1| + \cdots + |S_r| \leqslant \varepsilon^2 k$. In this case we set $X = Y_1 = \cdots = Y_r = W$, and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:book} to the colouring restricted to $W$ with $$p = \frac{1}{r} - 2\varepsilon, \qquad \mu = 2^{30} r^3, \qquad t = 2^{-40} r^{-3} k \qquad \text{and} \qquad m = R\big( k, \ldots, k, k - t \big).$$ In order to apply Theorem~\ref{thm:book}, we need to check that $t \geqslant \mu^5 / p^2$, and that $$|X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t} \qquad \text{and} \qquad |Y_i| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m.$$ The first two of these inequalities are both easy: the first holds because $k \geqslant 2^{200} r^{20}$, and for the second note that since $n \geqslant r^{rk/2}$ and $\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j| \leqslant rk/4$, we have $$|X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{rk/4} r^{rk/2} \geqslant r^{rk/4} \geqslant \big( 2^{61} r^7 \big)^{2^{-10} r k} \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t},$$ as required. The third inequality is more delicate: observe first\footnote{See Appendix~\ref{app:binomial} for a proof of the second inequality.} that $$R\big( k, \ldots, k, k-t \big) \leqslant \binom{rk-t}{k,\dots,k,k-t} \leqslant e^{-(r-1)t^2/3rk} r^{rk-t} \leqslant e^{-t^2/6k} r^{rk-t}.$$ and therefore, since $\delta \leqslant 2^{-10} t^2/k^2$ and $p = 1/r - 2\varepsilon \geqslant e^{-3\varepsilon r} / r$, we have $$n \geqslant e^{-\delta k} r^{rk} \geqslant r^t e^{t^2/8k} \cdot R\big( k, \ldots, k, k-t \big) \geqslant \frac{m}{p^t} \cdot \exp\bigg( \frac{t^2}{8k} - 3\varepsilon r t \bigg).$$ Moreover, by our choice of $t$ and $\mu$, we have $$\frac{t}{8k} = \frac{1}{2^{43} r^3} \geqslant \frac{1}{2^{47}r^3} + \frac{1}{2^{48}r^3} = \frac{2^{13} r^3}{\mu^2} + 4\varepsilon r.$$ Finally, since $\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j| \leqslant \varepsilon^2 k \leqslant \varepsilon t$, it follows that $$|Y_i| = |W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\varepsilon t} n \geqslant \frac{m}{p^t} \cdot \exp\bigg( \frac{t^2}{8k} - 4\varepsilon r t \bigg) \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m,$$ as claimed. Thus $\chi$ contains a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book, and hence, by our choice of $m$, $\chi$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Take the Erdős–Szekeres sets from Lemma 5.2; if they are large, Lemma 5.3 finishes. Otherwise apply the book theorem to $W$ with $p=1/r-2\varepsilon$, $\mu=2^{30}r^3$, $t=2^{-40}r^{-3}k$, $m=R(k,\dots,k,k-t)$.

nodes.name: Multinomial coefficient bound
nodes.statement: For each $k,t,r \in \mathbb{N}$ with $3 \leqslant t \leqslant k$, $$\binom{rk-t}{k,\dots,k,k-t} \leqslant e^{-(r-1)t^2/3rk} r^{rk-t}.$$
nodes.label: lem:multibounds

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.1
nodes.statement: To prove this, observe that $$\binom{rk-t}{k,\dots,k,k-t} \binom{rk}{k,\dots,k}^{-1} = \, \prod_{i = 0}^{t - 1} \frac{k - i}{rk - i} = r^{-t} \,\prod_{i = 0}^{t-1} \bigg( 1 - \frac{(r-1)i}{rk - i} \bigg) \leqslant r^{-t} \cdot e^{-(r-1)t^2/3rk}.$$ Since $\binom{rk}{k,\dots,k} \leqslant r^{rk}$, the claimed inequality follows.
nodes.statement_short: Compare with $\binom{rk}{k,\dots,k}$: the ratio is a product of $t$ factors each at most $r^{-1}(1-(r-1)i/(rk-i))$.

nodes.name: Observe that all moments of the inner products are positive
nodes.statement: The idea of the proof is as follows. We will first observe (see Lemma~\ref{lem:moments}) that all of the moments of the inner products $\langle \sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U') \rangle$ are positive.
nodes.statement_short: Observe that all moments of the inner products are positive
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Define a special function with non-negative Taylor coefficie
nodes.statement: The key step is then to define a function $f \colon \mathbb{R}^r \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ (see~\eqref{def:f}) whose Taylor expansion has non-negative coefficients, that is only positive close to the positive quadrant, and that does not grow too fast.
nodes.statement_short: Define a special function with non-negative Taylor coefficients
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Conclude by a simple calculation
nodes.statement: With this function in hand, the lemma will then follow from a simple calculation.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by a simple calculation
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Rewrite the product of inner products with an index sequence
nodes.statement: To simplify the notation, let us write $$\big\langle \sigma_1(U),\sigma_1(U') \big\rangle^{\ell_1} \cdots \big\langle \sigma_r(U), \sigma_r(U') \big\rangle^{\ell_r} = \prod_{i = 1}^\ell \big\langle \sigma_{a_i}(U), \sigma_{a_i}(U') \big\rangle $$ where $\ell = \ell_1 + \cdots + \ell_r$ and $(a_1,\dots,a_\ell)$ is such that $\big| \big\{ i \in [\ell] : a_i = j \big\} \big| = \ell_j$ for each $j \in [r]$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the product of inner products with an index sequence
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Introduce tensor products $Z, Z'$ whose inner product is the
nodes.statement: Now set $$Z = \sigma_{a_1}(U) \otimes \sigma_{a_2}(U) \otimes \cdots \otimes \sigma_{a_\ell}(U) \quad \text{and} \quad Z' = \sigma_{a_1}(U') \otimes \sigma_{a_2}(U') \otimes \cdots \otimes \sigma_{a_\ell}(U'),$$ and note that $$\big\langle Z, Z' \big\rangle = \prod_{i = 1}^\ell \big\langle \sigma_{a_i}(U), \sigma_{a_i}(U') \big\rangle,$$ since $\langle u_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes u_r, v_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes v_r \rangle = \langle u_1, v_1 \rangle \cdots \langle v_r , u_r \rangle $ for any vectors $u_i,v_i \in \mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce tensor products $Z, Z'$ whose inner product is the product
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Use independence: $\mathbb{E}\langle Z,Z'\rangle = \langle\m
nodes.statement: Finally, note that $Z$ and $Z'$ are independent and identically distributed random vectors, and therefore $$\mathbb{E} \big[ \langle Z, Z' \rangle \big] = \mathbb{E}_{Z'} \big[ \mathbb{E}_Z \big[ \langle Z, Z' \rangle \big] \big] = \mathbb{E}_{Z'} \big[ \big\langle \mathbb{E}[Z], Z' \big\rangle \big] = \big\langle \mathbb{E}[Z], \mathbb{E}[Z'] \big\rangle \geqslant 0,$$ as required, where the final inequality holds because $\mathbb{E}[Z] = \mathbb{E}[Z']$.
nodes.statement_short: Use independence: $\mathbb{E}\langle Z,Z'\rangle = \langle\mathbb{E}Z,\mathbb{E}Z'\rangle \ge 0$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Collect elementary facts about $2+\cosh\sqrt{x}$
nodes.statement: Observe first that $x \leqslant 2 + \cosh\sqrt{x} \leqslant 3e^{\sqrt{x}}$ for every $x \geqslant 0$, that $$f(x_1,\dots,x_r) = \bigg( \prod_{i = 1}^r \big( 2 + \cosh \sqrt{x_i} \big) \bigg) \sum_{j = 1}^r \frac{x_j}{2+\cosh\sqrt{x_j}},$$ and that $\cosh \sqrt{x} = \cos \sqrt{-x}$, and hence $-1 \leqslant \cosh \sqrt{x} \leqslant 1$ for all $x < 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Collect elementary facts about $2+\cosh\sqrt{x}$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Upper bound when all $x_i \ge -3r$
nodes.statement: It follows that \begin{equation} 1 \leqslant 2 + \cosh\sqrt{x} \leqslant 3e^{\sqrt{x+3r}} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \frac{x}{2+\cosh\sqrt{x}} \leqslant 1 \end{equation} for all $x \geqslant -3r$, and hence $$f(x_1,\dots,x_r)\leqslant r \prod_{i=1}^r 3e^{\sqrt{x_i + 3r}} = 3^r r \exp\bigg(\sum_{i=1}^r \sqrt{x_i + 3r} \bigg),$$ for every $x_1,\ldots,x_r \geqslant -3r$, as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound when all $x_i \ge -3r$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Show $f \le -1$ when some $x_i \le -3r$
nodes.statement: Moreover, if $x_i \leqslant -3r$, then, again using~\eqref{eq:cosh:bounds}, $$\sum_{j = 1}^r \frac{x_j}{2+\cosh\sqrt{x_j}} \leqslant \frac{x_i}{3} + r - 1 \leqslant - 1.$$ Since $2 + \cosh \sqrt{x} \geqslant 1$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, it follows that $f(x_1,\dots,x_r) \leqslant -1$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Show $f \le -1$ when some $x_i \le -3r$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Set $Z_i$ and get $\mathbb{E}f(Z)\ge0$ from Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: For each $i \in [r]$, define $Z_i = 3r\big\langle \sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U') \big\rangle$, and observe that, by Lemma~\ref{lem:moments} and linearity of expectation, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\big[ f\big( Z_1,\ldots,Z_r \big) \big] \geqslant 0, \end{equation} since all of the coefficients of the Taylor expansion of $f$ are non-negative.
nodes.statement_short: Set $Z_i$ and get $\mathbb{E}f(Z)\ge0$ from Lemma 3.2
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Split the expectation over $E$ and $E^c$ using Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:special:function}, it follows that if we define $E$ to be the event that $Z_i \geqslant -3r$ for every $i \in [r]$, then \begin{equation} 3^r r \cdot \mathbb{E}\bigg[ \exp\bigg( \sum_{i = 1}^r \sqrt{ Z_i + 3r } \bigg) \mathbf{1}_E \bigg] \geqslant 1 - \mathbb{P}(E), \end{equation} where $\mathbf{1}_E \in \{0,1\}$ denotes the indicator of the event $E$, since the left-hand side bounds the contribution to the expectation on the left-hand side of~\eqref{eq:Ex:f:positive} due to the event $E$, and the right-hand side bounds the contribution to the expectation due to the event $E^c$.
nodes.statement_short: Split the expectation over $E$ and $E^c$ using Lemma 3.3
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Case $\mathbb{P}(E)\ge\beta$: take $\lambda=-1$
nodes.statement: The result now follows from a simple calculation. First, note that $$\mathbb{P}(E) = \mathbb{P}\Big( Z_i \geqslant - 3r \, \text{ for all } \, i \in [r] \Big),$$ so if $\mathbb{P}(E) \geqslant \beta$, then the claimed inequality holds with $\lambda = -1$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $\mathbb{P}(E)\ge\beta$: take $\lambda=-1$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Claim for the case $\mathbb{P}(E)\le\beta$: inequality (9) h
nodes.statement: We claim that if $\mathbb{P}(E) \leqslant \beta$, then there exists $\lambda \geqslant -1$ such that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \geqslant \beta r e^{-C\sqrt{\lambda + 1}}, \end{equation} where $M = \max \big\{ \big\langle \sigma_i(U),\sigma_i(U') \big\rangle : i \in [r] \big\}$, and therefore (by the union bound) there exists an $i \in [r]$ as required. To see this, set $f(x) = e^{c \sqrt{x + 1}}$ with $c = \sqrt{3}r^{3/2}$, and observe that $$\mathbb{E}\big[ f(M) \mathbf{1}_E \big] \, \leqslant \, \mathbb{P}(E) + \int_{-1}^\infty \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \cdot f'(\lambda) \,\mathrm{d}\lambda$$ since $f(-1) = 1$ and if $E$ holds then $M \geqslant -1$. It follows that if $\mathbb{P}(E) \leqslant \beta$ and~\eqref{eq:max:big:and:E} does not hold for any $\lambda \geqslant -1$, then \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[ \exp\big( c \sqrt{M + 1} \big) \mathbf{1}_E \Big] & \leqslant \, \mathbb{P}(E) + \int_{-1}^\infty \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \cdot \frac{c}{2\sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \cdot e^{c \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \,\mathrm{d}\lambda\\ & \leqslant \, \beta + \beta r \int_{-1}^\infty \frac{c}{2\sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \cdot e^{- \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \,\mathrm{d}\lambda \, \leqslant \, \beta (cr + 1), \end{align*} where in the second step we used our choice of $C = 4r^{3/2} \geqslant c + 1$, and in the final step we used the fact that $\int_0^\infty \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} e^{-\sqrt{x}} \, \mathrm{d}x = 1$. In particular, recalling that $\beta = 3^{-4r}$, it follows that the left-hand side of~\eqref{eq:eventE:inequality} is at most $3^r r \cdot 3^{-4r} \big( \sqrt{3}r^{5/2} + 1 \big) \leqslant 1/2$, which contradicts our assumption that $\mathbb{P}(E) \leqslant \beta$. Hence there exists $\lambda \geqslant -1$ such that~\eqref{eq:max:big:and:E} holds, as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Claim for the case $\mathbb{P}(E)\le\beta$: inequality (9) holds for some $\lambda$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Introduce $f(x)=e^{c\sqrt{x+1}}$ and its tail integral
nodes.statement: To see this, set $f(x) = e^{c \sqrt{x + 1}}$ with $c = \sqrt{3}r^{3/2}$, and observe that $$\mathbb{E}\big[ f(M) \mathbf{1}_E \big] \, \leqslant \, \mathbb{P}(E) + \int_{-1}^\infty \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \cdot f'(\lambda) \,\mathrm{d}\lambda$$ since $f(-1) = 1$ and if $E$ holds then $M \geqslant -1$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $f(x)=e^{c\sqrt{x+1}}$ and its tail integral
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Assuming (9) fails, bound $\mathbb{E}[e^{c\sqrt{M+1}}1_E] \l
nodes.statement: It follows that if $\mathbb{P}(E) \leqslant \beta$ and~\eqref{eq:max:big:and:E} does not hold for any $\lambda \geqslant -1$, then \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[ \exp\big( c \sqrt{M + 1} \big) \mathbf{1}_E \Big] & \leqslant \, \mathbb{P}(E) + \int_{-1}^\infty \mathbb{P}\Big( \big\{ M \geqslant \lambda \big\} \cap E \Big) \cdot \frac{c}{2\sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \cdot e^{c \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \,\mathrm{d}\lambda\\ & \leqslant \, \beta + \beta r \int_{-1}^\infty \frac{c}{2\sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \cdot e^{- \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} \,\mathrm{d}\lambda \, \leqslant \, \beta (cr + 1), \end{align*} where in the second step we used our choice of $C = 4r^{3/2} \geqslant c + 1$, and in the final step we used the fact that $\int_0^\infty \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} e^{-\sqrt{x}} \, \mathrm{d}x = 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Assuming (9) fails, bound $\mathbb{E}[e^{c\sqrt{M+1}}1_E] \le \beta(cr+1)$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Contradict (8)
nodes.statement: In particular, recalling that $\beta = 3^{-4r}$, it follows that the left-hand side of~\eqref{eq:eventE:inequality} is at most $3^r r \cdot 3^{-4r} \big( \sqrt{3}r^{5/2} + 1 \big) \leqslant 1/2$, which contradicts our assumption that $\mathbb{P}(E) \leqslant \beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Contradict (8)
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Conclude (9) holds
nodes.statement: Hence there exists $\lambda \geqslant -1$ such that~\eqref{eq:max:big:and:E} holds, as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude (9) holds
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Define normalised neighbourhood vectors $\sigma_i(x)$
nodes.statement: For each colour $i \in [r]$, define a function $\sigma_i \colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{Y_i}$ as follows: for each $x \in X$, choose a set $N'_i(x) \subset N_i(x) \cap Y_i$ of size exactly $p_i|Y_i|$, where $p_i = p_i(X,Y_i)$, and set $$\sigma_i(x) = \frac{\hbox{$1\mkern-6.5mu1$}_{N'_i(x)} - p_i\hbox{$1\mkern-6.5mu1$}_{Y_i}}{\sqrt{\alpha_ip_i|Y_i|}},$$ where $\hbox{$1\mkern-6.5mu1$}_S \in \{0,1\}^{Y_i}$ denotes the indicator function of the set $S$.
nodes.statement_short: Define normalised neighbourhood vectors $\sigma_i(x)$
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Translate inner products into common-neighbourhood sizes
nodes.statement: Note that, for any $x,y\in X$, $$\big\langle \sigma_i(x),\sigma_i(y) \big\rangle \geqslant \lambda \quad \Leftrightarrow \quad |N'_i(x) \cap N'_i(y)|\geqslant \big( p_i + \lambda\alpha_i \big) p_i |Y_i|.$$
nodes.statement_short: Translate inner products into common-neighbourhood sizes
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Apply the geometric lemma
nodes.statement: Now, by Lemma~\ref{lem:lambda}, there exists $\lambda \geqslant -1$ and a colour $\ell \in [r]$ such that $$\mathbb{P}\Big( \big\langle \sigma_\ell(U),\sigma_\ell(U') \big\rangle \geqslant \lambda \, \text{ and } \, \big\langle \sigma_i(U), \sigma_i(U') \big\rangle \geqslant -1 \, \text{ for all } \, i \ne \ell \Big) \geqslant \beta e^{- C\sqrt{\lambda + 1}}.$$ where $U$, $U'$ are independent random variables distributed uniformly in the set~$X$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the geometric lemma
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Pick $x$ and $X'$ by averaging
nodes.statement: Hence there exists a vertex $x \in X$ and a set $X' \subset X$ such that, $$|X'| \geqslant \beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda + 1}} |X| \qquad \text{and} \qquad |N'_\ell(x) \cap N'_\ell(y)| \geqslant \big( p_\ell + \lambda\alpha_\ell \big) p_\ell |Y_\ell |$$ for every $y \in X'$, and $$|N'_i(x) \cap N'_i(y)|\geqslant \big( p_i - \alpha_i \big) p_i |Y_i|$$ for every $y \in X'$ and $i \in [r]$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick $x$ and $X'$ by averaging
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Set $Y'_i = N'_i(x)$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Setting $Y'_i = N'_i(x)$ for each $i \in [r]$, it follows that $$p_\ell\big( X', Y'_\ell \big) \geqslant p_\ell(X,Y_\ell) + \lambda \alpha_\ell \qquad \text{and} \qquad p_i\big( X', Y'_i \big) \geqslant p_i(X,Y_i) - \alpha_i$$ for every $i \in [r]$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Set $Y'_i = N'_i(x)$ and conclude
nodes.section: 3 The Proof of the Key Lemma

nodes.name: Unchanged $Y_i$: $p_i$ does not decrease
nodes.statement: Note first that if $Y_i(s+1) = Y_i(s)$, then $p_i(s+1) \geqslant p_i(s)$, since the minimum degree does not decrease when we take a subset of $X(s)$.
nodes.statement_short: Unchanged $Y_i$: $p_i$ does not decrease

nodes.name: Colour step: lose a factor $(1-1/t)$
nodes.statement: When we perform a colour step in colour $i$, we have $p_i(s+1) \geqslant p_i(s) - \alpha_i(s)$, by Lemma~\ref{key:lemma}, and hence $$p_i(s+1) - p_0 + \delta \geqslant \bigg( 1 - \frac{1}{t} \bigg) \big( p_i(s) - p_0 + \delta \big),$$ by our choice of $\alpha_i(s)$.
nodes.statement_short: Colour step: lose a factor $(1-1/t)$

nodes.name: Density-boost step: gain a factor $(1+\lambda/t)$
nodes.statement: Similarly, when we perform a density-boost step in colour $i$ we have $p_i(s+1) \geqslant p_i(s) + \lambda(s) \alpha_i(s)$, by Lemma~\ref{key:lemma}, and hence $$p_i(s+1) - p_0 + \delta \geqslant \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(s)}{t} \bigg) \big( p_i(s) - p_0 + \delta \big).$$
nodes.statement_short: Density-boost step: gain a factor $(1+\lambda/t)$

nodes.name: Multiply over steps
nodes.statement: Recalling that there are at most $t$ colour steps in colour $i$, and that $p_i(0) \geqslant p_0$, by the definition~\eqref{def:p0} of $p_0$, the claimed bound follows.
nodes.statement_short: Multiply over steps

nodes.name: Colour step shrinks $X$ by $\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: If $\lambda(j) \leqslant \lambda_0$, then by~\eqref{eq:key:ell} and Step~2 of the algorithm we have $$|X(j+1)| \geqslant \frac{\beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda_0 + 1}}}{r} \cdot |X(j)| - 1 = \varepsilon |X(j)| - 1.$$
nodes.statement_short: Colour step shrinks $X$ by $\varepsilon$

nodes.name: Density-boost step shrinks $X$ by $\beta e^{-C\sqrt{\lambda+
nodes.statement: On the other hand, if $\lambda(j) > \lambda_0$, then $j \in \mathcal{B}(s)$, and we have $$|X(j+1)| \geqslant \beta e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda(j) + 1}} |X(j)|,$$ by~\eqref{eq:key:ell} and Step~3 of the algorithm.
nodes.statement_short: Density-boost step shrinks $X$ by $\beta e^{-C\sqrt{\lambda+1}}$

nodes.name: Combine over at most $rt$ colour steps
nodes.statement: Since there are at most $rt$ colour steps, and $\beta \geqslant \varepsilon$, the claimed bound follows.
nodes.statement_short: Combine over at most $rt$ colour steps

nodes.name: Product condition (13) from Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Observe first that, by Lemma~\ref{lem:pi:lower:bound}, we have \begin{equation} \frac{\delta}{4} \prod_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(j)}{t} \bigg) \leqslant 1 + \delta \end{equation} for each $i \in [r]$.
nodes.statement_short: Product condition (13) from Lemma 4.1

nodes.name: Range of $\lambda(j)$
nodes.statement: Note also that $\lambda_0 \leqslant \lambda(j) \leqslant 5t/\delta$ for every $j \in \mathcal{B}(s)$, where the lower bound holds by the definition of $\mathcal{B}(s)$, and the upper bound by~\eqref{eq:B:condition} and since $\delta \leqslant 1/4$.
nodes.statement_short: Range of $\lambda(j)$

nodes.name: Ratio bound (14)
nodes.statement: Now, since $\log(1+x) \geqslant \min\{ x/2,1\}$ for all $x > 0$, it follows that \begin{equation} \frac{ \sqrt{\lambda(j)} }{\log(1 + \lambda(j)/t) } \leqslant \max\bigg\{ \frac{ 2t }{ \sqrt{\lambda_0} }, \, \sqrt{ \frac{5t}{\delta}} \bigg\} \leqslant \frac{ 3t }{ \sqrt{\lambda_0} }, \end{equation} where in the second inequality we used our assumption that $t \geqslant \lambda_0 / \delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Ratio bound (14)

nodes.name: Sum over $\mathcal{B}_i(s)$
nodes.statement: It now follows that $$\sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \sqrt{\lambda(j)} \leqslant \frac{ 3t }{ \sqrt{\lambda_0} } \sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}_i(s)} \log \bigg( 1 + \frac{\lambda(j)}{t} \bigg) \leqslant \frac{7 \log(1/\delta)}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}} \cdot t,$$ where the first inequality holds by~\eqref{eq:not:convexity}, and the second follows from~\eqref{eq:B:condition}, since $\delta \leqslant 1/4$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $\mathcal{B}_i(s)$

nodes.name: Sum over colours
nodes.statement: Summing over $i \in [r]$, we obtain the claimed bound.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over colours

nodes.name: Recall the hypotheses
nodes.statement: Recall that we are given an $r$-colouring $\chi$ of $E(K_n)$ and a collection of sets $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_r \subset V(K_n)$ with \begin{equation} |X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t} \qquad \text{and} \qquad |Y_i| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m \end{equation} for each $i \in [r]$, for some $p \in (0,1]$, $\mu \geqslant 2^{10} r^3$ and $t,m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $t \geqslant \mu^5 / p^2$, and moreover \begin{equation} |N_i(x) \cap Y_i| \geqslant p|Y_i| \end{equation} for every $x \in X$ and $i \in [r]$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the hypotheses

nodes.name: Choose $\delta$, $\lambda_0$ and state the goal
nodes.statement: We will run the multicolour book algorithm with \begin{equation} \delta = \frac{p}{\mu^2} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \lambda_0 = \bigg( \frac{\mu \log(1/\delta)}{8C} \bigg)^2, \end{equation} where $C = 4r^{3/2}$ (as before), and show that it ends with $$\max \big\{ |T_i(s)| : i \in [r] \big\} = t \qquad \text{and} \qquad \min\big\{ |Y_i(s)| : i \in [r] \big\} \geqslant m,$$ and therefore produces a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\delta$, $\lambda_0$ and state the goal

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|$ by Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: To do so, we just need to bound the sizes of the sets $X(s)$ and $Y_i(s)$ from below. Observe that $t \geqslant \lambda_0$ and $\delta \leqslant 1/4$, and therefore, by Lemma~\ref{lem:Bi:max}, that \begin{equation} |\mathcal{B}_i(s)| \, \leqslant \, \frac{4 \log(1/\delta)}{\lambda_0} \cdot t \, = \, \frac{2^{12} r^3}{\mu^2 \log(1/\delta)} \cdot t \, \leqslant \, t \end{equation} for every $i \in [r]$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|$ by Lemma 4.3

nodes.name: Lower bound on $|Y_i(s)|$ via Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: Since $p_0 \geqslant p$, by~\eqref{eq:book:thm:min:degree} and the definition of $p_0$, it follows that $$|Y_i(s)| \, \geqslant \, \bigg( p - \frac{3\delta}{4} \bigg)^{t + |\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} |Y_i| \, \geqslant \, e^{-2\delta t / p} \, p^{|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} \, \big( e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2} \big)^t \, m,$$ where the first inequality holds by Lemma~\ref{lem:Y:lower:bound}, and the second by~\eqref{eq:book:thm:conditions} and~\eqref{eq:Bi:final:bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound on $|Y_i(s)|$ via Lemma 4.4

nodes.name: Conclude $|Y_i(s)|\ge m$
nodes.statement: Noting that $p^{|\mathcal{B}_i(s)|} \geqslant e^{-2^{12} r^3 t / \mu^2}$, by~\eqref{eq:Bi:final:bound}, and that $\delta / p = 1/\mu^2$, it follows that $$|Y_i(s)| \, \geqslant \, e^{-2 t / \mu^2} \big( e^{2^{12} r^3 / \mu^2} \big)^t \, m \, \geqslant \, m,$$ as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude $|Y_i(s)|\ge m$

nodes.name: Bound $\varepsilon^{rt+|\mathcal{B}(s)|}$
nodes.statement: To bound $|X(s)|$, recall~\eqref{eq:X:lower:bound} and observe that $$\varepsilon^{rt + |\mathcal{B}(s)|} \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\beta}{r} \cdot e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda_0 + 1}} \bigg)^{2rt} \geqslant \big( e^{- 4C \sqrt{\lambda_0}} \big)^{rt} = \delta^{\mu r t/2} = \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{-\mu r t / 2},$$ where the first step holds because $\varepsilon = (\beta / r) e^{- C \sqrt{\lambda_0 + 1}}$ and $|\mathcal{B}(s)| \leqslant rt$, by~\eqref{eq:Bi:final:bound}, the second step holds because $\beta = 3^{-4r}$ and $\lambda_0 \geqslant 2^{10} r^3$, and the third and fourth steps follow from our choice of $\lambda_0$ and $\delta$ in~\eqref{def:delta:lambda0}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\varepsilon^{rt+|\mathcal{B}(s)|}$

nodes.name: Lemmas 4.5 and 4.6 give $|X(s)|>0$
nodes.statement: Moreover, observe that $t \geqslant \lambda_0 / \delta$, and therefore $$\sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}(s)} \sqrt{\lambda(j)+1} \leqslant \frac{8r \log(1/\delta)}{\sqrt{\lambda_0}} \cdot t = \frac{2^6Crt}{\mu},$$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:sum:of:lambdas} and our choice of $\lambda_0$, and therefore $$|X(s)| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t / 2} \exp\bigg( - \frac{2^6C^2rt}{\mu} \bigg) - rt > 0,$$ for every $s \in \mathbb{N}$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:X:lower:bound} and since $\mu \geqslant 2^{10} r^3$ and $C = 4r^{3/2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 4.5 and 4.6 give $|X(s)|>0$

nodes.name: The algorithm produces the book
nodes.statement: It follows that the algorithm produces a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book, as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: The algorithm produces the book

nodes.name: Base case: $n\le r$ or $r=1$
nodes.statement: We use induction on~$n$. Note that if $n \leqslant r$ or $r = 1$, then the sets $S_1 = \cdots = S_r = \emptyset$ and $W = V(K_n)$ have the required properties.
nodes.statement_short: Base case: $n\le r$ or $r=1$

nodes.name: Find a vertex with large degree in some colour $j$
nodes.statement: We may therefore assume that $n > r \geqslant 2$, and that there exists a vertex $x \in V(K_n)$ and a colour $\ell \in [r]$ such that $$|N_\ell(x)| < \bigg( \frac{1}{r} - \varepsilon \bigg) n - 1,$$ and hence there exists a different colour $j \ne \ell$ such that $$|N_j(x)| \geqslant \frac{1}{r-1} \bigg( n - \bigg( \frac{1}{r} - \varepsilon \bigg) n \bigg) \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1 + \varepsilon}{r} \bigg) n.$$
nodes.statement_short: Find a vertex with large degree in some colour $j$

nodes.name: Apply induction inside $N_j(x)$
nodes.statement: Applying the induction hypothesis to the colouring induced by the set $N_j(x)$, we obtain sets $S'_1,\ldots,S'_r$ and $W'$ satisfying the conclusion of the lemma with $n$ replaced by $|N_j(x)|$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply induction inside $N_j(x)$

nodes.name: Add $x$ to $S_j$ and check the size bound
nodes.statement: Setting $$W = W', \qquad S_j = S'_j \cup \{x\} \qquad \text{and} \qquad S_i = S'_i \qquad \text{for each } \, i \ne j,$$ we see that $W$ satisfies the minimum degree condition (by the induction hypothesis), and $$|W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\sum_{i = 1}^r |S'_i|}|N_j(x)| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\sum_{i=1}^r |S_i|}n.$$
nodes.statement_short: Add $x$ to $S_j$ and check the size bound

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $(S_i,W)$ is a monochromatic book in colour~$i$ for each $i \in [r]$, it follows that $S_1,\dots,S_r$ and $W$ are sets with the claimed properties.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude

nodes.name: Set parameters and take sets from Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: Given $r \geqslant 2$, set $\delta = 2^{-160} r^{-12}$, let $k \geqslant 2^{200} r^{20}$ and $n \geqslant e^{-\delta k} r^{rk}$, and let $\chi$ be an arbitrary $r$-colouring of $E(K_n)$. Set $\varepsilon = 2^{-50} r^{-4}$, and let $S_1,\ldots,S_r$ and $W$ be the sets given by Lemma~\ref{lem:ESz:steps}.
nodes.statement_short: Set parameters and take sets from Lemma 5.2

nodes.name: Case many Erdős–Szekeres steps: Lemma 5.3 gives $K_k$
nodes.statement: Suppose first that $|S_1| + \cdots + |S_r| \geqslant \varepsilon^2 k$, and observe that, by Lemma~\ref{lem:many:ESz:steps} and our lower bounds on $n$ and $|W|$, we have $$|W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j|} e^{-\delta k} r^{rk} \geqslant R_r\big( k - |S_1|, \ldots, k - |S_r| \big).$$ Since $(S_i,W)$ is a monochromatic book in colour~$i$ for each $i \in [r]$, it follows that there exists a monochromatic copy of $K_k$ in $\chi$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Case many Erdős–Szekeres steps: Lemma 5.3 gives $K_k$

nodes.name: Case few steps: apply the book theorem on $W$
nodes.statement: We may therefore assume from now on that $|S_1| + \cdots + |S_r| \leqslant \varepsilon^2 k$. In this case we set $X = Y_1 = \cdots = Y_r = W$, and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:book} to the colouring restricted to $W$ with $$p = \frac{1}{r} - 2\varepsilon, \qquad \mu = 2^{30} r^3, \qquad t = 2^{-40} r^{-3} k \qquad \text{and} \qquad m = R\big( k, \ldots, k, k - t \big).$$ In order to apply Theorem~\ref{thm:book}, we need to check that $t \geqslant \mu^5 / p^2$, and that $$|X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t} \qquad \text{and} \qquad |Y_i| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m.$$ The first two of these inequalities are both easy: the first holds because $k \geqslant 2^{200} r^{20}$, and for the second note that since $n \geqslant r^{rk/2}$ and $\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j| \leqslant rk/4$, we have $$|X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{rk/4} r^{rk/2} \geqslant r^{rk/4} \geqslant \big( 2^{61} r^7 \big)^{2^{-10} r k} \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t},$$ as required. The third inequality is more delicate: observe first\footnote{See Appendix~\ref{app:binomial} for a proof of the second inequality.} that $$R\big( k, \ldots, k, k-t \big) \leqslant \binom{rk-t}{k,\dots,k,k-t} \leqslant e^{-(r-1)t^2/3rk} r^{rk-t} \leqslant e^{-t^2/6k} r^{rk-t}.$$ and therefore, since $\delta \leqslant 2^{-10} t^2/k^2$ and $p = 1/r - 2\varepsilon \geqslant e^{-3\varepsilon r} / r$, we have $$n \geqslant e^{-\delta k} r^{rk} \geqslant r^t e^{t^2/8k} \cdot R\big( k, \ldots, k, k-t \big) \geqslant \frac{m}{p^t} \cdot \exp\bigg( \frac{t^2}{8k} - 3\varepsilon r t \bigg).$$ Moreover, by our choice of $t$ and $\mu$, we have $$\frac{t}{8k} = \frac{1}{2^{43} r^3} \geqslant \frac{1}{2^{47}r^3} + \frac{1}{2^{48}r^3} = \frac{2^{13} r^3}{\mu^2} + 4\varepsilon r.$$ Finally, since $\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j| \leqslant \varepsilon^2 k \leqslant \varepsilon t$, it follows that $$|Y_i| = |W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\varepsilon t} n \geqslant \frac{m}{p^t} \cdot \exp\bigg( \frac{t^2}{8k} - 4\varepsilon r t \bigg) \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m,$$ as claimed. Thus $\chi$ contains a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book, and hence, by our choice of $m$, $\chi$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Case few steps: apply the book theorem on $W$

nodes.name: Set $X=Y_i=W$ and choose $p,\mu,t,m$
nodes.statement: We may therefore assume from now on that $|S_1| + \cdots + |S_r| \leqslant \varepsilon^2 k$. In this case we set $X = Y_1 = \cdots = Y_r = W$, and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:book} to the colouring restricted to $W$ with $$p = \frac{1}{r} - 2\varepsilon, \qquad \mu = 2^{30} r^3, \qquad t = 2^{-40} r^{-3} k \qquad \text{and} \qquad m = R\big( k, \ldots, k, k - t \big).$$
nodes.statement_short: Set $X=Y_i=W$ and choose $p,\mu,t,m$

nodes.name: List the conditions to check
nodes.statement: In order to apply Theorem~\ref{thm:book}, we need to check that $t \geqslant \mu^5 / p^2$, and that $$|X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t} \qquad \text{and} \qquad |Y_i| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m.$$
nodes.statement_short: List the conditions to check

nodes.name: Check $t\ge\mu^5/p^2$ and the size of $X$
nodes.statement: The first two of these inequalities are both easy: the first holds because $k \geqslant 2^{200} r^{20}$, and for the second note that since $n \geqslant r^{rk/2}$ and $\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j| \leqslant rk/4$, we have $$|X| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{rk/4} r^{rk/2} \geqslant r^{rk/4} \geqslant \big( 2^{61} r^7 \big)^{2^{-10} r k} \geqslant \bigg( \frac{\mu^2}{p} \bigg)^{\mu r t},$$ as required.
nodes.statement_short: Check $t\ge\mu^5/p^2$ and the size of $X$

nodes.name: Bound $m$ with Lemma A.1 and relate to $n$
nodes.statement: The third inequality is more delicate: observe first\footnote{See Appendix~\ref{app:binomial} for a proof of the second inequality.} that $$R\big( k, \ldots, k, k-t \big) \leqslant \binom{rk-t}{k,\dots,k,k-t} \leqslant e^{-(r-1)t^2/3rk} r^{rk-t} \leqslant e^{-t^2/6k} r^{rk-t}.$$ and therefore, since $\delta \leqslant 2^{-10} t^2/k^2$ and $p = 1/r - 2\varepsilon \geqslant e^{-3\varepsilon r} / r$, we have $$n \geqslant e^{-\delta k} r^{rk} \geqslant r^t e^{t^2/8k} \cdot R\big( k, \ldots, k, k-t \big) \geqslant \frac{m}{p^t} \cdot \exp\bigg( \frac{t^2}{8k} - 3\varepsilon r t \bigg).$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $m$ with Lemma A.1 and relate to $n$

nodes.name: Compare exponents
nodes.statement: Moreover, by our choice of $t$ and $\mu$, we have $$\frac{t}{8k} = \frac{1}{2^{43} r^3} \geqslant \frac{1}{2^{47}r^3} + \frac{1}{2^{48}r^3} = \frac{2^{13} r^3}{\mu^2} + 4\varepsilon r.$$
nodes.statement_short: Compare exponents

nodes.name: Check the size of $Y_i$
nodes.statement: Finally, since $\sum_{j = 1}^r |S_j| \leqslant \varepsilon^2 k \leqslant \varepsilon t$, it follows that $$|Y_i| = |W| \geqslant \bigg( \frac{1+\varepsilon}{r} \bigg)^{\varepsilon t} n \geqslant \frac{m}{p^t} \cdot \exp\bigg( \frac{t^2}{8k} - 4\varepsilon r t \bigg) \geqslant \bigg( \frac{e^{2^{13} r^3 / \mu^2}}{p} \bigg)^t \, m,$$ as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Check the size of $Y_i$

nodes.name: Book plus choice of $m$ gives $K_k$
nodes.statement: Thus $\chi$ contains a monochromatic $(t,m)$-book, and hence, by our choice of $m$, $\chi$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Book plus choice of $m$ gives $K_k$
